posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
@21f2000709 The test cases for BPT3.4 seem to be working perfectly fine and works for all test cases with the correct solution script.

If you only read the test case files you will get the wrong idea. You have to read the evaluation_file.sh along with the test cases to understand that it is not providing you paths outside your home directory, thus you will not get any access denied issue. The path outputed by your script is later substituted to look like a path outside your home. Read the eval script to learn more if you are interested and have studied till sed. Otherwise, simply follow the instructions, it will not give you any permission error.


(if you are interested to learn how to output the path without getting substituted by the eval script, ping in this thread after BPT3 deadline is over)

Make sure you are following the problem statement correctly and are writing your script inside script.sh in ~/se2001/BPT3_problem_4 and are using the argument $1 provided to your script for finding all the files and deleting the empty ones. Do not attempt to read the test case files directly.

Regards,
Sayan

posts.cooked:
But sir, when i give argument the given path ‘/path/to/directory/’
It gives error that no such file or directory is present.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
If you give the literal path /path/to/directory/ to the script it will say no such directory is present. It is a placeholder for the actual path, not a path itself. Just like we say <insert your name> when filling out forms, of course your name is not <insert your name>, it means you are to put your name there.

You should run the script by using synchro eval, you don’t need to give any path as argument by yourself. It is done automatically by synchro.

Your work is to simply create the script.

Ohh, thanks a lot

But sir, just for clarification when we give argument $1, it means that we have to pass the value.
But here it is present in the question statement so need not to be.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
$1 inside a shell script means you are using the first argument that is passed to that shell script through command line.

If you are running the script yourself, yes, you have to provide the argument, after the name of the command.

However, as stated earlier, for VM tasks, you do not run the script.sh by yourself (you can if you want to check if its working), rather you call synchro eval which runs the evaluation_file.sh script which inturn will call your script.sh. The argument is passed from there, it is not absent.

If you are interested, I would recommend going through the /opt/se2001/BPT3_problem_4/evaluation_file.sh file, which is run when you type synchro eval for BPT3_problem_4, to understand exactly how the eval script validates your script.

Now that you have covered shell scripts (W6+W7), you should have the faculty (and hopefully also the curiosity) to go through all the evaluation scripts of all the assigments to try to understand how exact the evaluation is done, and how shell scripts are written. If you see something that you do not understand, copy that and paste it into ChatGPT and ask it to explain what the part of script is doing exactly. This is one of the positive usecases of AI.

If you have any doubts related to the evaluation script, do let us know here as well. Will be happy to clarify.

Regards,
Sayan
